one_line_reason: Multiple RCT meta-analyses show oral Lycium barbarum (goji) supplementation affecting lipid/glucose metabolism in general adult populations, the kind of outcome consumers buy it for.

selected.intervention: L. barbarum (goji berry) oral supplementation vs placebo/control
selected.dose_as_stated: not stated (meta-analysis pools multiple RCT doses)
selected.primary_outcome: lipid profile (triglycerides, HDL-C, total cholesterol, LDL-C)
selected.why_selected: Recent meta-analysis of RCTs in general adults showing significant TG decrease and HDL-C increase from oral goji supplementation

selected.intervention: Lycium barbarum polysaccharide (LBP) oral supplementation vs control
selected.primary_outcome: serum triglycerides, fasting blood glucose, LDL and HDL
selected.why_selected: Meta-analysis showing significant effects on glucose and lipid markers; note this isolates LBP (the polysaccharide extract) rather than whole berry

selected.intervention: L. barbarum oral supplementation vs control
selected.primary_outcome: cardiometabolic risk factors (fasting glucose, total cholesterol, triglycerides, bodyweight, blood pressure)
selected.why_selected: Significant reduction in fasting glucose but non-significant trends for lipids and no effect on bodyweight/blood pressure; useful for calibrating the strength of the glucose claim

selected.intervention: Standardized Lycium barbarum juice (GoChi®) 120 mL/day, oral
selected.primary_outcome: self-reported general well-being (fatigue, stress, sleep quality, mental acuity, etc.)
selected.why_selected: Positive general well-being outcome closer to how goji is marketed, but the exposure is a specific branded standardized juice product

blockers: 34213407 and part of the underlying RCTs in 37773857/28401234 study Lycium barbarum polysaccharide (LBP), a standardized extract, which may not correspond to whole dried goji berry or juice products in the catalog
22897500 studies a specific branded standardized juice (GoChi®, 120 mL/day) the catalog likely does not carry, and dose is a liquid volume that may not map to a label amount
None of the selected meta-analyses state a single consistent dose in the abstract, complicating dose-to-label mapping

excluded_pmids.reason: Systematic review of neuroprotective therapies in retinitis pigmentosa, a clinical eye-disease population; Lycium barbarum's modest benefit is from a single phase II trial cited within the review (very low certainty), not a primary source and not general supplement use
Nutritional intervention review for Sjogren disease (a clinical autoimmune population); Lycium barbarum polysaccharide appears mainly in animal models, not as isolated human efficacy evidence
Qiming granules, a multi-herb traditional Chinese medicine combination product (8 herbs); not a single-ingredient goji exposure
Review of LBP in osteoarthritis; evidence is described as in vitro/in vivo animal models with an explicit lack of human disease-modifying evidence
General review of LBP therapeutic potential across many conditions; only 2 RCTs are cited and the authors state further large-scale trials are needed, not established human efficacy
Chemical constituents of the Lycium genus; a phytochemistry catalog, not an efficacy study
RCT of Lycium barbarum extract in varicocele patients, a clinical male-infertility population rather than general supplement use
RCT of a combination extract (Agastache rugosa + Ficus carica + Lycium barbarum) for skin aging; not a single-ingredient goji exposure
